trailheadDirection: From Grand Coulee drive south on Highway 155, or from Coulee City drive north on it. Most of the frozen flows sit between mileposts 8 and 17, and you can pull off on the shoulder or in a pullout beside the one you want.
approach: From the SR 155 roadside pullouts, walk the short distance to the flow you chose; nearly all of them can be seen from the road. Many finish in thick brush, so carry clippers or build a v-thread before the top.
note: MP area page for Banks Lake ice; one page, general SR 155 roadside parking

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38, turn right at the bottom of the ramp, and follow SE Homestead Valley Road around and under the I-90 overpass to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side) lot. A Discover Pass is required.
approach: From the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side), head toward the Neverland sign and keep left on the newer path. The wall is about 15 minutes from the lot.
note: Wayne's World MP page plus Exit 38 parent page (Far Side lot, Discover Pass)

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38, turn right at the bottom of the ramp, and follow SE Homestead Valley Road around and under the I-90 overpass to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side) lot. A Discover Pass is required.
approach: From the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side), walk toward Neverland and fork left onto the newer path. Dark Side is the first wall you meet, just to the right of a large dead cedar. Top-rope anchors are reached by crossing in front of and around the Wayne's World wall.
note: Dark Side MP page plus Exit 38 parent page

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38, turn right at the bottom of the ramp, and follow SE Homestead Valley Road around and under the I-90 overpass to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side) lot. A Discover Pass is required.
approach: From the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead (Far Side), walk to the left end of the Wayne's World wall and go up the fixed ladder there. At the top of the ladder turn left to reach the base of this wall. It takes about 20 minutes from the car.
note: Excellent Adventure Wall MP page plus Wayne's World page and Exit 38 parent page

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38 and follow SE Homestead Valley Road to Forest Service Road 9020, just before the road passes under I-90. Drive about 0.2 miles up FS 9020 to a pullout on the right.
approach: From the FS 9020 pullout, follow the old closed road south, then west toward the scree field below the wall. Stay on the road until you reach a small chopped log, turn uphill there, and follow a faint path to the base. Plan on under 20 minutes.
note: Black Ice Crag MP page; a trip report agrees on FS 9020 and a 0.2 mile approach

trailhead: Lincoln Park lot on Southeast Blvd
trailheadDirection: From Perry Street heading south, turn left onto 18th, which becomes Southeast Boulevard. The small, poorly signed lot is in the trees on the left about 0.5 miles along.
approach: From the Lincoln Park lot on Southeast Blvd, take the paved path and keep right at the first fork. At the next fork go right for the base of the cliff (left leads to the top). The base is roughly 400 ft beyond that second fork.

trailheadDirection: Drive to Alpental and park in the upper Alpental lot.
approach: From the Upper Alpental lot, follow the Snow Lake trail when there is little snow, cutting around the Source Lake bowl. In winter follow the ski and boot tracks along the south side of the stream to Source Lake, then head up. Go past Bryant Buttress on climber's left and look for the overhanging rock with bolts.
note: Rap Wall MP page only; no road directions beyond the upper Alpental lot

trailhead: Deception Crags and Mt Washington trailhead
trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38, turn right at the bottom of the ramp onto SE Homestead Valley Road, and take the next right onto the gravel road up a small hill to the trailhead. A Discover Pass is required.
approach: From the Deception Crags and Mt Washington trailhead, walk up to the Iron Horse Trail and turn right. About 20 seconds along, a short bolted face is on the left; 20 seconds beyond it a short steep path with tree roots leaves the trail on the left. Climb it to a big log, then up the steep slope to the wall. Loose blocks hide under the moss on the way down.
note: Roadhouse MP page says park for Deception Crags; lot taken from Exit 38 parent page

trailheadDirection: Turn off Highway 2 onto Whitepine Road and drive about 1 mile to parking just before the road runs under the railroad trestle.
approach: From Whitepine Road trestle parking, do not walk across the trestle, since trains come without warning. Continue on foot along the road beneath it and over Nason Creek on a small bridge. Just past the bridge turn back to the main wall across the creek, or climb the steep slope right of the talus for about 10 minutes to the main ice. Allow 15 to 20 minutes in all.

trailheadDirection: From Bellingham take Highway 542 to Glacier, then go another 13.3 miles and turn left onto the unpaved Hannegan Pass Road just before the Nooksack River bridge near milepost 46. Drive about two minutes and park on the left.
approach: From Hannegan Pass Road roadside, the routes are right beside the road, so there is no real walk.
note: Shuksan Crag MP page only; a search snippet of another page said a picnic-area walk, not opened
routes: Dry When Wet, AKA The Roof

trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 15 and drive south on 17th about 3 miles to a small pullout with room for about 5 cars.
approach: From the 17th Avenue pullout, take the climbers' path that forks left just after the gate. The wall is about a two-minute walk.

trailheadDirection: Heading north on Highway 155, look for a large pullout on the right 1.3 miles past the left turn into Steamboat Rock State Park.
approach: From the Devils Punch Bowl pullout (SR 155), hike down into the basin, then up to the east toward the ice. Put a helmet on before the approach, because large icicles drop from the overhung cliff above.
note: Devils Punch Bowl MP page; Banks Lake ice page agrees on SR 155 roadside parking

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 47 and follow Denny Creek Road to the Franklin Falls trailhead when the road is open and free of snow. It is usually closed in winter; then a Sno-Park permit is needed for the pullout on the north side of eastbound I-90.
approach: From the Franklin Falls trailhead, the falls are about a 5 minute walk. If you start from the I-90 pullout because the road is closed, expect closer to an hour.

trailheadDirection: From the Pullman-Moscow Highway, turn off at the stoplight onto Terre View Drive and park there. Do not park on the highway shoulder, and check whether a parking permit applies where you pull off.
approach: From Terre View Drive parking, walk toward the traffic signal and turn left at it. Keep going about five minutes until you reach the rock wall cut for the highway, where the ice forms. The wall is right beside traffic.

trailhead: Upper Mt. Baker Ski Area lot
trailheadDirection: Drive Highway 542 to its end and park in the Upper Mt. Baker Ski Area lot.
approach: From the Upper Mt. Baker Ski Area lot, take the Backcountry Access Trail and cut across above Chair 2, watching for skiers. Never come in from the top: the slopes above are closed and climbers risk a ticket for setting top-ropes from there. The area is closed whenever the nearby chairlifts are closed for avalanche control.
note: Pan Dome Falls Area MP page only, includes ski-area rules
